title: The Record High Diesel Prices
text:
The Record High Diesel Prices

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 7 Sep 2026

Because of soaring crack spreads, diesel prices everywhere around the world are making new all-time highs, at least in nominal terms. In real terms, diesel prices are still far below the levels reached in 2008 (when the Sichuan-Gansu earthquake, and consequent mobilizing of the Chinese rail system to bring rescuers and supplies into Western China meant that coal could no longer travel around the country, thereby pushing Chinese factories to rely on diesel generators), or in late 2011/early 2012 (when the Fukushima tsunami pushed Japan and Germany to shut down their nuclear plants). In real terms, the diesel price is still lower than the 2022 spike that followed the start of the Ukraine war.But even in “real terms,” the US diesel price is now over US$5/gallon (it is higher than that across most of the OECD). And above US$5/gallon, few good things happen. Trucking goods around becomes expensive, as does farming, shipping, mining, construction etc... As we never tire of pointing out, “economic activity is energy transformed,” and large parts of the economy find it much easier to generate activity, and profits, when the price of diesel is low than when it is high.
